transcript:
Agent: Good morning, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi, I’m Priya. I got your number from a friend — Shruti Joshi. She had her flat done by you in Aundh.
Agent: Of course — thank you for calling. What are you looking to do?
Caller: We have a 3BHK in Kothrud — Dahanukar Colony. We bought it two years ago and it still looks like the builder flat. We want to redo the whole thing — kitchen, living room, both bedrooms.
Agent: That sounds like a complete redesign. How big is the apartment?
Caller: About 1,400 sq ft carpet.
Agent: And your timeline?
Caller: We’d like to be done by March. We’re in no rush.
Agent: Perfect. Are you the owner?
Caller: Yes — myself and my husband. He knows we’re calling and is happy to go ahead.
Agent: Lovely. Can I take your number and schedule a consultation?
Caller: Sure. (gives number)

assessment.scope_summary: Full 3BHK redesign — kitchen, living, both bedrooms

decision_maker.evidence: Owner; husband aware and happy to go ahead

assessment.handoff_note:
Priya — 3BHK, ~1,400 sq ft carpet, Dahanukar Colony, Kothrud.
Bought 2 yrs ago, still builder finish. Wants full redesign: kitchen, living room, both bedrooms.
Timeline: done by March, relaxed.
Referral from Shruti Joshi (Aangan client, Aundh). Owner; husband on board.

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi. I was looking at your work on Instagram. I have a 2BHK in Wakad — can you tell me roughly how much something like that would cost?
Agent: Our pricing depends on the materials and the scope — the best way to get a clear picture is a consultation with one of our designers, who can walk you through everything. What are you planning to do?
Caller: Full redesign — modular kitchen, wardrobes, living room, both bedrooms. About 950 sq ft.
Agent: Good scope. What’s your timeline?
Caller: We move in November — so maybe starting design from October?
Agent: That works well. Shall I set up a consultation?
Caller: Yes, but can you give me a rough ballpark first? Even a range?
Agent: I genuinely can’t — it varies quite a bit based on materials. Giving you a number without seeing the site would be misleading. The designer will go through all of that with you — the consultation is free and there’s no obligation.
Caller: Okay, fair enough. Let’s book it.

assessment.timeline: Design from October; moving in November
open_questions: Is November move-in fixed? Execution may run past it
assessment.scope_summary: 2BHK full redesign — modular kitchen, wardrobes, living, bedrooms

real_project.evidence: Full redesign incl. modular kitchen and wardrobes

assessment.handoff_note:
2BHK in Wakad, ~950 sq ft. Full redesign: modular kitchen, wardrobes, living room, both bedrooms.
Wants to start design in October; moving in November — set expectations on execution time.
Found us on Instagram. Pushed hard for a price range — expect pricing questions early.

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, Aangan Studio.

Caller: Alright, understood. Thanks.

service_area.evidence: Site is in Nashik — outside Pune/PCMC

assessment.handoff_note: Suresh Patil — Nashik, home office + study. Outside service area; declined politely.

transcript:

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi, I’m calling about a commercial project. We’re a startup — just got our first proper office space in Baner. About 800 sq ft. We need workstations for 20 people, a small cabin, a meeting room, and a break area.
Agent: We do commercial fitouts up to about 3,000 sq ft. What’s the state of the space right now?
Caller: Bare shell — just columns and floor. Nothing else.
Agent: Full fitout from scratch. And the timeline?
Caller: We want to be operational by December. Our team is working from home currently.
Agent: December is doable. Are you the decision-maker for this?
Caller: Yes, I’m the founder.
Agent: Perfect. Let’s set up a consultation.

assessment.scope_summary: Startup office fitout — 20 workstations, cabin, meeting room, break area
assessment.handoff_note:
Startup founder — first office in Baner, ~800 sq ft bare shell.
Needs 20 workstations, 1 cabin, meeting room, break area. Team WFH until then.
Target: operational by December. Decision-maker on the call.

transcript:
Agent: Good morning, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hello — I want to redo my living room and kitchen before Diwali. Can you take it up?
Agent: Diwali is about three weeks away. Our design phase alone takes 3–4 weeks, and execution follows. We couldn’t do justice to a project in that time.
Caller: Even just the living room?
Agent: Even so — a room redesign with execution takes at least 8–10 weeks from start to finish. We wouldn’t want to rush it.
Caller: What if I start after Diwali?
Agent: A November start would work well. Shall I note your details for that?
Caller: Let me think and call back.

open_questions: Would a November start work? Caller said they would think and call back
assessment.scope_summary: Living room and kitchen before Diwali

timeline.evidence: Needs it done in ~3 weeks, before Diwali

assessment.handoff_note: Wanted living room + kitchen done before Diwali (~3 weeks). Not feasible; suggested a November start. Caller to call back.

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi. I have a 1BHK in Kharadi — about 550 sq ft. I want to do the kitchen and one bedroom. My budget is 1 to 1.5 lakh maximum for everything. Is that possible with you?
Agent: I appreciate you sharing that. For a kitchen redesign and a bedroom with full execution — materials, furniture, and contractor work — 1 to 1.5 lakh would be significantly below what a project of that scope would cost with us.
Caller: Even for one bedroom?
Agent: Even for one room. I wouldn’t want to bring you to a consultation if the numbers don’t align. I’d suggest checking with local contractors who work at that price point.
Caller: Okay, thank you for being straight.

budget.evidence: Volunteered ₹1–1.5 lakh for kitchen + bedroom — clearly below scope

assessment.handoff_note: 1BHK in Kharadi — kitchen + bedroom with a ₹1–1.5 lakh cap. Misalignment explained kindly on the call; not forwarded.

transcript:
Agent: Good morning, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi — I have a question. I’m in a rented apartment. Can you still take up a project?
Agent: It depends on the scope. What are you looking to do?
Caller: It’s a 2BHK in Baner. I’ve been here a year, I have a 3-year lease, and the place is quite bare. I want to properly design the living room, bedroom, and kitchen — no structural changes, just design and fittings.
Agent: That’s fine — we’ve done rented apartments before. For the kitchen we’d do a modular unit that can come out cleanly. The rest is largely flooring, lighting, and furniture — all reversible. Have you checked with your landlord?
Caller: Yes — they’re fine with it as long as we don’t break walls.
Agent: Perfect. No wall-breaking from us. Shall we set up a consultation?
Caller: Yes please.

assessment.scope_summary: Rented 2BHK — living room, bedroom, kitchen (no structural changes)

decision_maker.evidence: Tenant with 3-yr lease; landlord has agreed

assessment.handoff_note:
Tenant in a 2BHK in Baner (3-year lease, 1 year in). Wants living room, bedroom and kitchen designed — no structural work.
Landlord OK as long as no walls are broken; plan a removable modular kitchen.
Timeline not discussed.

transcript:
Agent: Good morning, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi — I run a small coworking space. I have a 180 sq ft pod I want to make look really nice. Good lighting, a nice desk, some storage. Can you help?
Agent: Our commercial projects are typically 500 sq ft or more. A 180 sq ft pod is below our minimum scope.
Caller: Not even for a smaller fee?
Agent: It’s not about the fee — it’s that our design and execution team is set up for a certain scale. A 180 sq ft space isn’t one we could do well at the quality we’d want to promise. I’d suggest a local designer who specialises in smaller commercial spaces.
Caller: Fair enough. Thanks.

assessment.scope_summary: 180 sq ft coworking pod — lighting, desk, storage
assessment.handoff_note: 180 sq ft coworking pod — below viable commercial scope. Declined politely.

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, Aangan Studio.
Caller: Hi — I’m planning to open a restaurant in Koregaon Park. I’ve seen your work and I love it. Would you be able to design the interiors?
Agent: We appreciate you reaching out. Restaurant and hospitality interiors are outside our current scope — we focus on residential and office spaces. For a restaurant you’d need a studio that specialises in commercial hospitality, which has very different material and compliance requirements.
Caller: Do you know anyone you could refer?
Agent: I don’t have a specific referral I could make confidently, but searching for hospitality interior designers in Pune would give you more relevant options.
Caller: Alright, thanks.

assessment.handoff_note: Restaurant in Koregaon Park — hospitality is out of scope. Declined politely.
